title: Battle.net launcher data
whyItMatters: The per-user Battle.net folder holds the launcher config and cache. It shows which Blizzard account was signed in on this machine.
source: Blizzard Support, Deleting Battle.net Files (article 34719): machine-wide data in C:/ProgramData/Battle.net - https://us.battle.net/support/en/article/34719
notes: Machine-wide launcher cache and agent data. The per-user %APPDATA%/Battle.net config folder is not covered. Files are counted, never opened or parsed.

cleanup.signOut: Sign out in the Battle.net launcher, so the Blizzard account stops keeping a signed-in session on this machine.
steps: Sign out in the Battle.net launcher.
Uninstall the launcher from Settings > Apps > Installed apps if the PC no longer needs it.
Leave the shared folder named in the plan to the full reset; it needs administrator rights to remove.
cleanup.risk: Removes the launcher and its cache from this PC. Games already installed by the launcher stay on disk and keep their files.
